title.narrative: Protection-Led Access to Integrated Health Services During the Lean Season in Monguno LGA in Borno State.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe GISCOR proposed project “Protection-Led Access to Integrated Health and Nutrition Services During the Lean Season” is a lifesaving humanitarian intervention in Monguno LGA in Borno State. Targeting a health facility (HF) in five wards of the LGA to deliver essential services to the vulnerable, especially to women, children, people with disabilities, and hard-to-reach populations through a combination of mobile clinics, community outreach, and supporting existing health facilities. The project follows the Sector-Wide Approach (SWAP), emphasising integrated lifesaving service delivery and the strengthening of community systems for long-term resilience. Community feedback mechanisms, regular monitoring, and local capacity building ensure accountability and sustainability. The project will prioritise primary health care services and mainstream WASH in health facilities and protection. The protection mainstreaming will be through complementarity with the existing GISOR BHA-funded project in Monguno. The proposed action will leverage the existing collaboration with the government and community, including implementing partners, to ensure holistic, high-quality essential service delivery. ltbrgt The health component provides primary healthcare through fixed sites and mobile teams, including disease surveillance, provision of essential drugs and supplies, immunisations, treatment of communicable and non-communicable diseases, mental health referral, and ambulance referrals. MoU with hospitals and the SPHCDA for secondary health care for acute emergencies to ensure patients receive quality health care services, including feeding, transportation, laboratory services, and medical cost coverage. Sexual and reproductive health services, including antenatal, skilled delivery, postnatal, and emergency obstetric care. Health workers will be trained in BeMONC, CCSAS, IMCI, drug use, and disease management. In addition, the intervention will also focus on nutrition screening for acute malnutrition in children under five and MIYCN for pregnant or breastfeeding women and girls (PBWG). SAM cases will be referred to therapeutic programmes for RUTF, and MAM cases for RUSF or complementary feeding. Vulnerable households shall be linked to supplemental nutrition assistance with integrated GBV and SEA messaging and referrals. While the WASH actions to be mainstreamed will improve access to safe water supplies, sanitation improvements, and hygiene promotion through hygiene stations, waste management in health facilities will be implemented using standard codes and IPC measures, and water chlorination and monitoring will be conducted regularly in HF. Protection will also serve as the entry point of the intervention. Using Protection Action Groups and local networks, the project activates early warning and community surveillance systems. Activities include protection monitoring, referral, and awareness campaigns addressing GBV and sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), with confidential reporting mechanisms encouraging safe disclosures.ltbrgtlt/pgt
